title: Microsoft Purview: apply sensitivity labels with user-defined permissions in Word, Excel and PowerPoint for the web
summary: The briefing's availability, prerequisites, licensing statements and governance controls are supported by the roadmap and Microsoft documentation. The label-editing path stops on the correct page but should include the final options already supplied in its note.

claims.claim: Office for the web supports applying sensitivity labels with user-defined permissions.
claims.quote: Office for the web in Microsoft 365 supports the application of sensitivity labels with user-defined permissions.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is April CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "April CY2026"

claims.claim: The release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Web support requires admin opt-in through enabling sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: How to enable sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive (opt-in)

claims.claim: User-defined permissions use Let users assign permissions when they apply the label with the Word, PowerPoint and Excel prompt selected.
claims.quote: User-defined permissions refers to an encryption configuration and the setting **Let users assign permissions when they apply the label** and the checkbox **In Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, prompt users to specify permissions** is selected.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: For this configuration the user rather than the administrator chooses who can access the document.
claims.quote: For this configuration, the user and not the administrator controls both who can access the document, and what permissions they have.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The user chooses the document permissions when applying the label.
claims.quote: In Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, when a user applies a sensitivity label that lets them assign permissions to a document, the user is prompted to specify their choice of users and permissions for the encryption.

claims.claim: The capabilities table marks custom permissions for users and groups in the web apps as Yes - opt-in.
claims.quote: Let users assign permissions:  - Prompt users for custom permissions (users and groups) ... [Yes - opt-in](sensitivity-labels-sharepoint-onedrive-files#support-for-labels-configured-for-user-defined-permissions)

claims.claim: The capabilities table marks custom permissions for users, groups and organisations in the web apps as Yes - opt-in.
claims.quote: Let users assign permissions:  - Prompt users for custom permissions (users, groups, and organizations) ... [Yes - opt-in](sensitivity-labels-sharepoint-onedrive-files#support-for-labels-configured-for-user-defined-permissions)

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: After SharePoint and OneDrive sensitivity-label support is enabled, labels with this configuration are displayed in Office for the web.
claims.quote: Labels with this configuration are displayed in Office for the web.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft asks administrators to enable encrypted-file co-authoring before users select these labels or change the label in the browser.
claims.quote: Before users select these labels to specify users and permissions, or change the label applied, make sure you've [enabled co-authoring for files encrypted with sensitivity labels](sensitivity-labels-coauthoring).

claims.claim: Office for the web lets users enter a domain name in the permissions prompt.
claims.quote: For labeling in Windows and using Office for the web, users can additionally specify a domain name when they're prompted to specify their choice of users and permissions.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A domain entry grants the selected rights across the owning organisation's Microsoft Entra domains, not just the named domain or sales subdomain.
claims.quote: Because Contoso Corporation owns the contoso.com domain, all users in that domain and all other domains that the organization owns in Microsoft Entra ID will be granted read access.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Typing @ in Office for the web offers a selectable entry for everybody in the organisation.
claims.quote: When you use Office for the web, typing the @ character automatically displays a selectable entry for everybody in the organization.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Relabelling a user-defined-permissions file with a label that does not apply encryption removes the original encryption rather than preserving it.
claims.quote: If an existing file that's labeled with user-defined permissions is relabeled with a sensitivity label that doesn't apply encryption, the original encryption is removed rather than preserved.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope: Users; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Users must be in scope of a publishing policy for the configured label to be available for selection.
claims.quote: Until you publish your labels, they won't be available to select in apps or for services. To publish the labels, they must be added to a label policy.

claims.claim: Office for the web does not prevent screen captures of encrypted documents.
claims.quote: For encrypted documents in Office for the web, [screen captures aren't prevented](azure-rights-management-learn-about#can-rights-management-prevent-screen-captures).

claims.claim: For labelled and encrypted documents, Office for the web blocks copying to the clipboard when the Copy usage right is not granted.
claims.quote: when documents are labeled and encrypted, and the **Copy**[usage right](rights-management-usage-rights) isn't granted, Office for the web prevents copying to clipboard in the same way as desktop apps prevent this action.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: An external guest whose user-defined label permissions come through a group in their home tenant cannot open the file in Office for the web or from SharePoint or OneDrive in desktop Office.
claims.quote: users from an external tenant can't open files protected with a user-defined permissions sensitivity label in Office for the web. The same limitation also applies when users open the file from SharePoint or OneDrive with Microsoft Office desktop applications.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft's workaround is to grant permissions directly to the external user.
claims.quote: Grant permissions directly to the external user in the sensitivity label.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft also allows adding the external user to a group in the resource tenant and granting that group permissions.
claims.quote: Add the external user to a group in the contoso tenant, and grant permissions to that contoso tenant group in the sensitivity label.

claims.claim: A label that lets users assign permissions can be recommended.
claims.quote: A sensitivity label that lets users assign permissions can be recommended to users, but can only be automatically applied for the Do Not Forward and Encrypt-Only options.

claims.claim: Automatic application of labels that let users assign permissions is limited to the Outlook Do Not Forward and Encrypt-Only options, rather than the document prompt.
claims.quote: A sensitivity label that lets users assign permissions can be recommended to users, but can only be automatically applied for the Do Not Forward and Encrypt-Only options.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[2].note; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Enabling co-authoring changes the format and location of labelling metadata in Word, Excel and PowerPoint files.
claims.quote: The change that this setting makes is the metadata format and location for Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft warns against enabling co-authoring while apps, services, scripts or tools read or write metadata at the old location.
claims.quote: Don't enable this setting if you use any apps, services, scripts, or tools that read or write labeling metadata to the old location.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; controls[2].note
claims.claim: Once enabled, encrypted-file co-authoring cannot be disabled in the Microsoft Purview portal and requires PowerShell to disable.
claims.quote: After you enable co-authoring for files with sensitivity labels for your tenant, you can't disable this setting in the Microsoft Purview portal. This action is supported only by using PowerShell.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive cannot process some desktop-labelled and encrypted files containing Power Query data, custom add-in data, custom XML parts or bibliographies; opening in desktop apps is a documented alternative.
claims.quote: For these files, either apply a label without encryption so that users can later open them in Office for the web, or instruct users to open the files in their desktop apps. Files that are labeled and encrypted only in Office for the web aren't affected.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Printing encrypted documents is not supported in Office for the web.
claims.quote: For encrypted documents, printing, downloading, exporting, and creating a copy aren't supported in Office for the web.

claims.claim: Downloading encrypted documents is not supported in Office for the web.
claims.quote: For encrypted documents, printing, downloading, exporting, and creating a copy aren't supported in Office for the web.

claims.claim: Exporting encrypted documents is not supported in Office for the web.
claims.quote: For encrypted documents, printing, downloading, exporting, and creating a copy aren't supported in Office for the web.

claims.claim: Creating a copy of an encrypted document is not supported in Office for the web.
claims.quote: For encrypted documents, printing, downloading, exporting, and creating a copy aren't supported in Office for the web.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The same service description also says sensitivity labelling, including automatic or policy-based labelling, requires Microsoft 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).

claims.claim: Administrators also need a licence to manage sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Admins also need a license to manage sensitivity labels.

claims.claim: The service description and Get started page do not document a meter for this Office for the web feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Office web user-defined permissions sensitivity label licensing meter pay as you go manual sensitivity labeling. Opened Get started with sensitivity labels and the service description's Information Protection sensitivity labeling section; no meter for this feature.

claims.claim: The Get started page's pay-as-you-go requirement concerns applying labels to non-Microsoft 365 data sources.
claims.quote: Specific to non-Microsoft 365 data sources, applying sensitivity labels in the Data Map and using protection policies requires you to set up [pay-as-you-go billing](purview-billing-models) in your organization.

claims.claim: Word .docx and .docm files in SharePoint and OneDrive support applying labels in Office for the web.
claims.quote:
Applying a sensitivity label in Office for the web or in SharePoint:
- **Word**: .docx, .docm

claims.claim: Excel .xlsx, .xlsm and .xlsb files support this web labelling surface.
claims.quote: - **Excel**: .xlsx, .xlsm, .xlsb

claims.claim: PowerPoint .pptx and .ppsx files support this web labelling surface.
claims.quote: - **PowerPoint**: .pptx, .ppsx

claims.claim: The Purview portal route for enabling SharePoint and OneDrive label support requires a global administrator.
claims.quote: You must sign in as a global administrator for your tenant.

claims.claim: The PowerShell route for enabling SharePoint and OneDrive label support requires SharePoint admin privileges.
claims.quote: Using a work or school account that has SharePoint admin privileges in Microsoft 365, connect to SharePoint.

claims.claim: Turning co-authoring on or off requires at least DLP Compliance Management or Information Protection Admin.
claims.quote: To turn this capability on or off, you need at least the DLP Compliance Management or Information Protection Admin role.

claims.claim: Security Administrator and Compliance Administrator are alternative co-authoring configuration roles.
claims.quote: Alternative roles include the Security Administrator and Compliance Administrator roles.

claims.claim: The SharePoint and OneDrive label-support setting takes about 15 minutes to take effect.
claims.quote: As with all tenant-level configuration changes for SharePoint and OneDrive, it takes about 15 minutes for the change to take effect.

claims.where: Scope: Timing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft says to wait 24 hours after enabling encrypted-file co-authoring.
claims.quote: Wait 24 hours for this setting to replicate across your environment before you use this new feature for co-authoring.

claims.where: Scope: Multi-Geo; controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Multi-Geo tenants must use PowerShell to enable label support in every geo-location.
claims.quote: If you have Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo, you must use PowerShell to enable this support for all your geo-locations.

claims.where: Scope: Out of scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Labels with User access to content expires set to anything other than Never are not displayed in Office for the web.
claims.quote: **User access to content expires** is set to a value other than **Never**. ... For labels with either of these encryption configurations, the labels aren't displayed to users in Office for the web.

claims.claim: Labels configured with Double Key Encryption are not displayed in Office for the web.
claims.quote: **Double Key Encryption** is selected. ... For labels with either of these encryption configurations, the labels aren't displayed to users in Office for the web.

claims.claim: Office for the web cannot open documents encrypted with an on-premises key, Double Key Encryption or encryption applied independently of a label such as a Rights Management template.
claims.quote: Documents that are encrypted in the following ways can't be opened in Office for the web: ... Encryption that uses an on-premises key ... Double Key Encryption ... Encryption that was applied independently from a label

claims.claim: Labelled and encrypted Office files larger than 12 MB copied to another site cannot be opened in Office for the web but can be opened in an Office client app.
claims.quote: When a labeled and encrypted Office file larger than 12 MB is copied or moved to a different site, SharePoint can no longer process this file.

claims.claim: The Purview path through Sensitivity labels, Edit label, scope and Control access reaches the Access control page for configuring user-defined permissions.
claims.quote: on the **Choose protection settings for the types of items you selected** page, make sure you select **Control access**. ... On the **Access control** page, select one of the following options
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > label > Edit label > Define the scope for this label > Files & other data assets > Choose protection settings for the types of items you selected > Control access > Access control > Configure access control settings > Let users assign permissions when they apply the label > In Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, prompt users to specify permissions'. The existing note already gives these final choices. The entry steps are supported by the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels.

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label> -EncryptionPromptUser $true sets the label's Word, Excel and PowerPoint user-defined-permissions option.
claims.quote: The EncryptionPromptUser parameter specifies whether to set the label with user defined permission in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. ... $true: The label is set with user defined permissions in Word, Excel and PowerPoint.

claims.claim: EncryptionPromptUser requires EncryptionProtectionType UserDefined.
claims.quote: This parameter is meaningful only when the EncryptionEnabled parameter value is either $true or $false, and when the EncryptionProtectionType parameter value is UserDefined.

claims.claim: Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Turn on now enables SharePoint and OneDrive label support; the prompt disappears once enabled.
claims.quote: **Solutions** > **Information Protection** > **Sensitivity labels**. ... select **Turn on now** ... The command runs immediately and when the page is next refreshed, you no longer see the message or button.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true enables sensitivity-label support for SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: To enable the new capabilities, use the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet with the EnableAIPIntegration parameter: ... Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true

claims.claim: The documented co-authoring switch is at Purview portal > Settings > Solution settings > Information Protection > Co-authoring for files with sensitivity labels > Turn on co-authoring for files with sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: **Settings** > **Solution settings** > **Information Protection** > **Co-authoring for files with sensitivity labels**. ... Then select **Turn on co-authoring for files with sensitivity labels**, and **Apply**

claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig -EnableLabelCoauth $true enables encrypted-document co-authoring support tenant-wide.
claims.quote: The EnableLabelCoauth parameter enables or disables co-authoring support in Office desktop apps for the entire organization. ... $true: Co-authoring support in Office desktop apps is enabled.

claims.claim: Purview portal > Audit > Search reaches the audit search page.
claims.quote: Select the **Audit** solution card. If the **Audit** solution card isn't displayed, select **View all solutions** and then select **Audit** from the **Core** section. ... On the **Search** page, configure the following search criteria

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog is the PowerShell operation for searching the unified audit log.
claims.quote: The underlying cmdlet used to search the audit log is an Exchange Online cmdlet, which is **Search-UnifiedAuditLog**. That means you can use this cmdlet to search the audit log instead of using the search tool

claims.claim: Applied sensitivity label to file records web application of a label as FileSensitivityLabelApplied.
claims.quote: Applied sensitivity label to file | FileSensitivityLabelApplied ... Office for the web, details pane in a SharePoint document library or the Files tab in Teams, or an auto-labeling policy (FileSensitivityLabelApplied)

claims.claim: Changed sensitivity label applied to file records a web label change as FileSensitivityLabelChanged.
claims.quote: Changed sensitivity label applied to file ... Office for the web, details pane in a SharePoint document library or the Files tab in Teams, or an auto-labeling policy (FileSensitivityLabelChanged)

claims.claim: Removed sensitivity label from file is an audit activity for label removal in Office for the web.
claims.quote: Removed sensitivity label from file | FileSensitivityLabelRemoved ... Office for the web, details pane in a SharePoint document library or the Files tab in Teams, or an auto-labeling policy (FileSensitivityLabelRemoved)

claims.claim: Publishing policies are reached at Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > **Solutions** > **Information Protection** > **Publishing policies**.

claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig with EnableLabelCoauth $false disables encrypted-file co-authoring.
claims.quote: Set-PolicyConfig -EnableLabelCoauth:$false

claims.claim: Disabling co-authoring loses labelling information in unencrypted Word, Excel and PowerPoint files that used the new metadata format.
claims.quote: The new metadata format and location for Office documents that were used while the setting was enabled won't be copied to the original format and location. As a result, this labeling information for unencrypted Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files will be lost.

claims.claim: Changes to encryption options for letting users assign permissions affect only newly labelled or relabelled items.
claims.quote: Whenever you change the encryption options for letting users assign permissions, that change only applies to newly labeled or relabeled items.

claims.claim: A separate documented way to keep these user-defined-permissions labels desktop-only while SharePoint and OneDrive label support remains enabled is not established.
claims.quote: Searched: sensitivity labels Office web user defined permissions disable only desktop web labels advanced settings. Read SharePoint/OneDrive label support and Manage sensitivity labels in Office apps search excerpts; found tenant integration and Windows-only switches, not this separate control.
